sentences.text: He seeks to cancel the bail granted to the first respondent as per the order in B.A. No.6572 of 2025 dated 27.06.2025.

Though this Court is not given the Roster for dealing with petitions under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the Hon'ble Chief Justice has posted this case before this Court for consideration as the original bail order was issued by this Court.

2. The second accused in Crime No.504 of 2025 of Varappuzha Police Station, who is arrayed as an accused alleging offences under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, had approached this Court in B.A.No.6572 of 2025.
After considering the matter on merits and after hearing the learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsel for the petitioner therein, anticipatory bail was granted subject to conditions.
3. Petitioner in this Crl.M.C, who is the de facto complainant in the crime alleges that the bail order was obtained after suppressing and misrepresenting material facts.

It is also alleged that fraud has been 2025:KER:74584 played upon this Court by the first respondent and hence, the bail granted to him ought to be cancelled.
4.

I have heard Sri.A.Ranjith Narayanan., the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri.Anandakrishnan K., the learned counsel for the first respondent as well as Sri.Noushad K A., the learned Public Prosecutor.

sentences.text:
In the order granting bail to the first respondent, it is specifically noticed that the learned Public Prosecutor had contended that the certificate of incorporation of 'JJTR Chits Private Limited'
indicated that it was a part of 'Safe Chit Fund' and the involvement of the accused was clearly evident.

Despite the said contention, which is almost identical to the contentions now raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner in this application, this Court had granted anticipatory bail to the first respondent herein on conditions.

6. While granting anticipatory bail, this Court had observed that the de facto complainant's specific contention was that he joined in the chit find scheme conducted by 'Safe Chit Fund', while the certificate of incorporation retrieved by the Investigating Officer showed the address of "JJTR Chits (P) Ltd." as Safe Chit Fund.
Despite the above, this Court noted that the said reference to Safe Chit Fund does not meant the company, 'JJTR Chits Private Limited' is a part of the establishment called 'Safe Chit fund'.
There was certainly a rider that it is a matter to be established during investigation.

The above observations in the order granting bail to the first respondent indicate that this Court had considered the contention regarding connection between Safe Chit Fund and JJTR Chits Private Limited for the purpose of considering the application for grant of anticipatory bail.
It cannot strictly be said that the said contention now raised by the petitioner herein was considered or not brought to the notice of the Court.

Since, despite considering the very same contentions now raised by the petitioner on the earlier occasion, on the basis of the submission of the learned Public Prosecutor and this Court granted bail, I am of the view that the order granting bail to the petitioner need not be cancelled.
8. In this context, it is worthwhile to refer to the decision in Himanshu Sharma v. State of Madhya pradesh [2024 KHC 8093], relating to the scope of cancellation of an order granting bail.

entities.text: Himanshu Sharma v. State of Madhya pradesh [2024 KHC 8093]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, I find no merit in this petition and it is dismissed.
